references.text: Moses' command to anoint Aaron and his sons for priestly service, the same anointing ritual described here.
Detailed description of the anointing of Aaron and his sons for priestly service.
God commands that Aaron and his sons be anointed to serve as priests.
The fulfillment of the command to anoint, where Moses anoints Aaron and his sons.
Reference to Aaron's sons who were anointed for priestly service.
The promise of an eternal priesthood, the same theme of a priesthood for all generations.
Messianic prophecy about an eternal priesthood in the order of Melchizedek.
The temporary nature of the Levitical priesthood compared to Christ's eternal priesthood.
Both verses confirm that anointing successors ensures an eternal priesthood through the generations.
Complementary perspective: while the source provides the basis for the service, this verse describes the holy status that follows from the anointing.
The source establishes the right to the service through anointing, while this verse protects that right from outsiders.
Direct reference to the same event (the day of anointing) and confirmation that the arrangement is eternal for all generations.
